title: MIS complexity on even-hole-free graphs
statement_text: What is the computational complexity of computing a maximum independent set in even-hole-free graphs?
context_text: The abstract describes this as a long-standing open question. From the hardness side, MIS is W[1]-hard for $C_4$-free graphs, while MIS is polynomial on perfect graphs; even-hole-free graphs sit between these two classes. The precise complexity (polynomial-time vs. NP-hard) remains unresolved.
paper_contribution: Proves that MIS is FPT when parameterized by the solution size $k$ in the class of even-hole-free graphs, by applying the augmenting-graph technique twice and reducing to a dynamic program on chordal graphs.
notes: Described as a 'long-standing open question' with no specific original attribution or citation in the text.
paper_title: The independent set problem is FPT for even-hole-free graphs

title: Open problem: Combinatorial algorithm for MIS on perfect graphs
statement_text: It remains an open question to find a combinatorial algorithm for the maximum independent set problem on perfect graphs. In fact, we do not even have a combinatorial FPT algorithm for the maximum independent set problem on perfect graphs.
context_text: A combinatorial algorithm here means one that does not rely on the ellipsoid method. A graph is perfect if every induced subgraph $H$ satisfies $\chi(H)=\omega(H)$; by the Strong Perfect Graph Theorem these are exactly the Berge graphs (no induced odd cycle of length at least $5$ and no induced complement of one). An FPT algorithm for maximum independent set parameterized by the solution size $k$ decides whether the input $n$-vertex graph has an independent set of size $k$ in time $f(k)n^{O(1)}$ for some computable $f$. Maximum independent set is polynomial-time solvable on perfect graphs by the ellipsoid method (Grötschel, Lovász and Schrijver), and combinatorially on subclasses such as bipartite, chordal and claw-free graphs. This open problem is mentioned as motivation: the paper studies the structurally similar class of even-hole-free graphs (no induced cycle of even length at least $4$), where the complexity of maximum independent set is a long-standing open question, and shows that maximum independent set is FPT parameterized by the solution size there, whereas it is W[1]-hard on graphs with no induced $C_4$.
notes: Stated as a known open problem in the community without a specific attribution cite; no labeled theorem environment.
paper_title: The independent set problem is FPT for even-hole-free graphs
